title: Migrate a long-running job from a status table and poller to AWS Lambda durable functions
description: Same job twice: a FastAPI app with a DynamoDB status table and poller, then the same app on an AWS Lambda durable function with checkpointed steps and retries.

introBox.headline: How it works
text: A job too long or too fragile for one Lambda invocation is usually run through a hand-rolled status table behind a FastAPI app: write a PENDING row, have a poller claim it, run the steps, update the row after each one, detect stale RUNNING rows, count attempts. This pattern deploys that version (before/) and the same job as a Lambda durable function (after/) side by side.

In the durable version each step is a context.step() call. The runtime checkpoints results, replays past completed steps after a crash, and retries the flaky step with RetryPresets.transient() instead of a hand-written attempt counter.

The public job id becomes the DurableExecutionName, so starting a job is idempotent and GET /jobs/{id} resolves job_id to an execution ARN and reads status with GetDurableExecution. Durable statuses are mapped back to the old API's words so clients do not change.
Cutover: point POST at /v2, keep GET polling as is. The /v2 GET still answers for old rows while the legacy poller drains them; delete the legacy functions once no rows lack an execution ARN.
The durable half has a local test using the SDK's in-memory runner, so the step wiring and retry can be verified without deploying.

bullets.text: Building fault-tolerant applications with Lambda durable functions

text: See the GitHub repo for detailed testing instructions, including a local test that needs no AWS account.
